pages.subtitle: Repairing broken cliffs, missing ground and visible chunk boundaries.

Matched cliff test, after: the artificial projections removed.

blocks.heading: Solid ground while detail arrives
blocks.text: Nearby terrain takes priority. Ground stays solid as chunks are replaced, and neighbouring surfaces meet instead of exposing blue slits. Smooth updates gradually change eligible distant slopes; interactive ground and riverbanks change immediately to preserve contact.

images.caption: Latest 191 km flight review, at a separate river location: continuous land and water into the distance; the flat surrounding ring is gone.

blocks.text: The reviewed high-speed flight found no missing ground in eight perspective checks. Distant terrain retains its broad relief while closer detail arrives. The approach that left a flat surrounding ring was removed. This is a coverage result, not proof of smooth frame times everywhere.

pages.title: Water, woodland and contact
pages.subtitle: Separate generated locations; the original reported world was unsaved.

images.caption: Earlier waterfall repair review: paired bank spikes removed. Final waterfall capture and player check pending.

blocks.text: Ground support follows the terrain triangles actually on screen. The actual player also stays above steep ground when an adjacent obstacle redirects them; this has passed in the canyon review. Riverbeds remain below the water in the checked channel interiors and boundaries.

images.caption: Fjord forest review, separate from the canyon and river flight: distant trees retain physical scale and upright silhouettes.

blocks.text: Trees anchor to the displayed ground as terrain changes. Distant forest colour reflects crown coverage; oversized tree cards were replaced. Tree placement is spread across frames without exposing incomplete groups, and completed placement matches the original trees exactly.

Still visible: some aerial forests look too sparse, leaf edges can look thin, and ground plants repeat. Canyon ledges also remain too evenly spaced. These are remaining appearance limits; the repair does not claim finished landscape art.

pages.title: Performance and limits
pages.subtitle: Latest completed measurements; final build results still pending.

blocks.text: 1080p, Medium vegetation, 6 km view; Chrome video shared the PC. Dry grassland flight: 200 m/s at 500 m altitude. Forest/savanna: 8 m/s travel with rapid turns. These are representative routes, not the worst place on the planet. p99 means 99% of frames were faster than that time. A strict 100 FPS minimum requires every frame below 10 ms: this remains unmet.

Latest jungle comparison: peak tree-ground correction fell from 7.262 to 3.696 ms, and scatter-ground correction from 6.051 to 2.700 ms. The 40.8 ms frame occurred outside the instrumented terrain work; its cause remains unidentified. These gains do not establish smoother worst frames overall.

Full-view total was about 48.1 seconds including preparation. This run used 60 FPS pacing and screenshot checks, so it measures loading and continuity rather than gameplay FPS. Startup still contains a noticeable first-time asset stall.
